newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SKODA SETS CZK.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SKODA SETS CZK.

text.p: Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. said on Friday it would set the issue price of its share issue of up to 2.5 billion crowns at 1,600 crowns per share, implying a 600 crown premium over nominal value in the first round of the offering.
Skoda shares, traded on the main market of the Prague Stock Exchange, rose five crowns on Friday to close at 980.
Skoda's shareholders approved the equity expansion at an extraordinary general meeting earlier on Friday to cover the firm's investment needs.
Skoda's current shareholders would have the right of first refusal for the offering. The firm's current basic capital is 9.48 billion crowns.
Skoda's largest shareholder is NERo s.r.o., owned by Skoda General Director Lubomir Soudek, with a 21.5 percent stake in Skoda.
The government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), holds a 8.7 percent stake in the company, but plans to sell it on the capital market soon.
Komercni Banka a.s. holds 11.7 percent together with one of its investment funds. Bank IPB a.s . holds a 5.9 percent stake.
Skoda is the country's largest engineering concern, based in the western city of Plzen. It is no longer affiliated with Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s.
Skoda's production ranges from beer cans to trucks, locomotives and power turbines.
